name: dpkg
description: The base package manager for .deb files: installs, removes, and inspects individual packages without dependency resolution.

flags.description: Install a local .deb file (dependencies must already be present).
List installed packages matching a pattern.
List files installed by a package.
Which package owns this file? (reverse lookup).
Configure all pending packages — the standard recovery command.

examples.explanation: Installs a downloaded .deb. If dependencies are missing, finish the job with sudo apt-get install -f.

examples.output: ii  nginx  1.24.0-2ubuntu7  amd64  high performance web server
examples.explanation: ii = installed OK. Other prefixes (rc = removed with config remnants, un = unknown) reveal package states.
Shows every file the nginx package placed on disk.
Finds which installed package provides a file.
Recovers from an interrupted apt/dpkg transaction — run this if apt complains about unconfigured packages.

about: dpkg is the foundation apt sits on. It never downloads from repositories and never resolves dependencies — apt does both by calling dpkg. Direct dpkg -i is for local .deb files, e.g. vendor downloads or debs built locally.
mistakes: Using dpkg -i for packages available in repositories — apt resolves dependencies, dpkg does not.
Panicking after a failed dpkg -i: run sudo apt-get install -f to fix dependencies.
